categories.main_business_segments: Pangrim Co., Ltd. primarily operates in the cotton textile manufacturing industry, producing cotton yarn, woven fabrics, and dyed fabrics. The company supplies these textile products mainly to large domestic and international apparel, sewing, and bedding companies. Additionally, it has diversified into medical and elderly care welfare services through its subsidiary Silverfree Co., Ltd. The company also engages in real estate leasing and sales.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes advanced spinning, weaving, dyeing, and printing technologies to produce high-value-added cotton textiles. It emphasizes eco-friendly and functional textile development, including recycled polyester, organic cotton, and waterless dyeing technologies. Production is carried out in an integrated system combining spinning, weaving, and processing, with facilities in Ansan, South Korea, and a subsidiary in Vietnam. The company also focuses on digital printing and special finishing techniques such as water-repellent and antibacterial treatments.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Pangrim serves large-scale domestic and international apparel manufacturers, sewing companies, and bedding product companies. Its major export markets include Europe, the United States, and Asia, with approximately 70% of sales derived from overseas buyers. Key overseas customers include JAFTEX Corporation, SNICKERS, KWINTET, HELLY HANSEN, and CANADA GOOSE. Domestic sales account for about 30%, including local brands and government procurement.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in South Korea with manufacturing facilities in Ansan and other locations. It has a wholly owned subsidiary, Pangrim Neotex Co., Ltd., in Vietnam, which handles integrated spinning, weaving, and processing. The company exports extensively to Europe, the United States, and Asia. It also maintains sales offices and agents in various international markets to support global distribution.
categories.supply_chain_position: Pangrim operates mainly in the midstream segment of the textile supply chain, focusing on spinning, weaving, dyeing, and finishing of cotton textiles. It sources raw cotton and yarns primarily from overseas suppliers in Brazil, the United States, China, India, and Pakistan. The company supplies intermediate textile products to downstream apparel and bedding manufacturers, positioning itself as a key material supplier in the textile industry.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company prioritizes R&D in eco-friendly and high-functionality textiles, including recycled and organic materials, waterless dyeing, and non-fluorine water repellents. It invests in digital printing and special finishing technologies to meet evolving fashion and environmental trends. Pangrim also focuses on developing products with certifications such as Oeko-Tex, GOTS, and GRS to capture the growing market for sustainable textiles. Additionally, it is expanding its medical and elderly care business as a diversification strategy.
categories.revenue_model: Pangrim generates revenue primarily through the sale of cotton textile products, including dyed and printed fabrics, to domestic and international apparel and bedding manufacturers. It also earns income from exporting raw cotton and yarns via its Vietnamese subsidiary. Additional revenue streams include real estate leasing and sales, as well as medical and elderly care services through its subsidiary Silverfree. The company’s sales are conducted via direct sales, local agents, and export contracts using L/C and T/T payment methods.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Pangrim competes with other major Korean textile companies such as Jeonbang, Dongil, Ilshin, Kyungbang, and Daehan Textile. The Korean cotton textile industry is highly competitive with pressures from low-cost producers in China, Pakistan, and Southeast Asia. Despite challenges, Pangrim maintains a strong market position through technological innovation, high-value product development, and overseas production investments. It is recognized as a leading domestic cotton textile manufacturer with a focus on quality and eco-friendly products.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of the fiscal year ending September 2024, Pangrim reported consolidated revenues of approximately 110.6 billion KRW, reflecting a 16% decline from the previous year due to reduced orders and rising raw material costs. The company experienced an operating loss of 3.27 billion KRW but achieved a net profit of 617 million KRW, reversing prior losses mainly due to financial asset gains. Total assets stood at 231.6 billion KRW with a healthy debt ratio of 22.1%, indicating stable financial health despite challenging market conditions. The company’s subsidiary in Vietnam showed declining sales and operating losses, reflecting global market pressures.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Pangrim differentiates itself by offering high-quality, eco-friendly, and functional cotton textiles that meet global sustainability standards and certifications. Its integrated production system from spinning to finishing enables consistent quality control and innovation. The company emphasizes advanced technologies such as digital printing, waterless dyeing, and special finishing treatments to provide unique textile solutions. Additionally, Pangrim’s strategic overseas production and diversified business portfolio, including medical and elderly care services, enhance its resilience and market competitiveness.
